response: Yes, higher body mass index (BMI) has been associated with worse asthma control in urban populations. Studies have shown that individuals with a higher BMI, particularly those who are obese, are more likely to experience poor asthma control, increased symptoms, and reduced lung function. This may be due to various factors, including increased inflammation, airway resistance, and decreased response to asthma medications. Additionally, urban populations may face unique challenges, such as environmental triggers and limited access to healthcare, which can further exacerbate the relationship between higher BMI and poor asthma control.
